results.notes:
The change has an off-by-one bug in `src/wrap.mjs`. The overflow check is `line.length + word.length > width`, which leaves out the separating space. It should be `line.length + 1 + word.length > width`.

For example, `wrap('aaa bbb', 6)` gives `['aaa bbb']`, a line of length 7 that is longer than the width of 6. No single word exceeds the width here, so this breaks the acceptance rule "No line is longer than `width`".

The tests don't catch it. The width-5 case uses two 5-letter words, which don't fit even without the space. The other case uses width 20, which is far too wide to exercise the boundary. No test sits at the exact boundary where the missing space matters.

The rest is fine. The code has no dependencies, no unsafe behavior and no changes outside the task. Whitespace handling, empty input and over-long words are all correct. The core wrapping rule is still wrong, so a maintainer shouldn't merge it as is.
